answer: Sybil resistance ties each challenge to a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse. A commit fixes the claimant and task parameters before the pulse; the later publicly verifiable signature supplies an unpredictable nonce, while reveal binds the response to that instance. Since no participant can forecast or bias the pulse before quorum formation, automated swarms cannot precompute solutions, farm offline, or recycle identities cheaply. Thus knoll, haven, and meadow remain randomized challenge labels, not exploitable work queues.
